subject-murieston-1586-1605-george-murei.assessment: Select George Glasgow-1099 as the leading possible existing identity for the Mureistoun man of 1586, probably the 1605 adult witness. His protocol-defined 1565–1572 birth range, minority in 1586 and 1598 marriage contract are real constraints, not a 1575 birthday or proof that 1598 was his first marriage. They permit the two occurrences. The 17 October family model prefers the record-defined George as James-991's probable father; identifying him with the merchant, and therefore William-3522 upstream, remains separately uncertain. James's unsupported circa-1575 estimate would conflict if proved, so no date is moved to force identity. Glasgow-3171's age-free 1676 burial implies exceptional longevity for a 1586 adult; Glascoe-36's reported 1589 death is unverified and would exclude the 1605 witness if confirmed. Retain both weak comparisons; no extra George son or mother is created.

subject-early-scotland-1650-issobell-gla.assessment: Select Issobell Glasgow-2454 as the best surviving possible existing identity: the Mid Calder 3 February 1648 baptism names father Wm, with Kirknewtonn residence, while the Haddington record states birth 24 and baptism 26 November 1639 to Wm Glasgow and Issobella Miral. The profile's rendered exact 1648 birth derives from a baptism/index and is not independently a birthday; a second or delayed baptism and regional movement are possible, not demonstrated. The nine-year and cross-parish difference keeps the match weak. Anderson-56713's actual account represents Issobell Anderson marrying Allexander Glasgow in Edinburgh in 1665, so this is a different birth-surname account, not evidence for a Glasgow-born child. It remains a remote comparison only if that surname history changes. Glasgow-3185's 1632 marriage concretely excludes the 1639 child. The Haddington parent–child statements remain direct at the documentary event level, independent of this later identification.

subject-early-scotland-1650-james-weaver.assessment: Select the documented Edinburgh weaver Glasgow-1150 as the leading possible 1646–1647 sasine identity: exact trade, region, 1641 apprenticeship and 1649 burgess admission fit the intervening property dates. His actual captured biography says born before the 1641 apprenticeship, not a proved 1620 birthday. Alexander's 1626 son Glasgow-3923 is a genuine local rival, but his father Alexander conflicts with the apprentice's explicitly named father Robert of Wester Duddingston: retain two profile accounts. James-991 could have changed trade, and James-3332's estimated 1634 birth is not a hard exclusion. Glasgow-3910 was dead by 1624, excluding a living 1646 role; an unread instrument could mention him as deceased predecessor. Alexander's residence is not automatically the weaver's, and no father–son relationship is supplied by shared references.

subject-carnwath-1524-1532-john-quothqua.assessment: Select Glasgow-1095 provisionally as the leading existing older-John comparison, using only the Saltmarket record-defined account maintained on its linked free-space page. John-1093 is a real rival, married by 1534 with an inferred circa-1510 birth; there is no concrete age exclusion. The current Hirmanscheillis dossier supersedes the input's November death reading with a qualified March reading; no alleged Andrew son is used. Consolidate all Quothquan John entries through October 1532; do not infer kinship with Thomas or a descent to James-3910.

subject-early-scotland-1650-robert-tanne.assessment: Select Robert Glasgow-1027 as the leading possible 1623 Glasgow tanner: he is the local adult and probable 1613 cordiner/burgess, with leather work and a documented Glasgow household through the 1620s. Cordiner and tanner are distinct occupations; compatibility is not an occupation identification. Robert-1156's age-free Duddingston burial in 1647 does not exclude him, but supplies a weaker place/trade comparison. The RPC passage has not been newly checked here; the 1630s payment men remain separate occurrence questions. Neither the tanner occupation nor Ninian parentage is newly proved by this candidate choice.

subject-carnwath-1524-1532-robert-carnwa.assessment: Select Glasgow-1096 as the leading possible existing Robert because his sourced Glasgow-burgh career gives the nearest Scottish comparison. Activity from 1551 to after February 1580 would require an earlier birth and long adult career if he was the 1524 litigant; circa 1520 is an estimate, not a conflict. Holkham Robert-4063 remains a real rival: the actual profile has no birth year, and the reported 23 March 1559 Old Style death corresponds to 1560, not an exclusion from 1524. No Norfolk–Carnwath bridge is known, which lowers preference without excluding him. The debt/grain award does not state Robert's occupation, residence or kin, and is not a reason to attach him to Quothquan John or Thomas.
